# aws-data-protection

Data-protection posture measured from dumps: KMS rotation on customer-managed keys only, Secrets Manager rotation (metadata, never values), S3 public-access-block and default-encryption posture, and private DNS on interface VPC endpoints.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-SEC-107` — Customer-managed KMS key has rotation disabled (high)

`KeyManager: CUSTOMER` with `KeyRotationEnabled: false` leaves the same material wrapping data indefinitely — rotation is one flag and the dump declares both fields.

Remediation: Enable automatic rotation (`EnableKeyRotation`) on symmetric CMKs; AWS-managed keys are excluded by construction of the measure.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotate-keys.html

### `AF-SEC-108` — Secrets Manager secret has rotation disabled (medium)

`RotationEnabled: false` means the credential's lifetime is unbounded — a leak has no expiry. The describe output declares the flag.

Remediation: Attach a rotation Lambda with a window matching the credential's exposure risk, or record why the secret legitimately never rotates.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_overview.html

### `AF-SEC-109` — S3 bucket public access block is incomplete or absent (critical)

All four `PublicAccessBlock` flags must be true to close the public surface; any false or a missing configuration is measured the same — `public_access_blocked` is only true when all four are set.

Remediation: Enable all four public-access-block flags at bucket level (or account level) unless the bucket is deliberately public — recorded as a decision, never assumed.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html

### `AF-SEC-110` — S3 bucket declares no server-side encryption configuration (medium)

A missing `ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration` is recorded as measured absence (the API's named error becomes the artifact); buckets created after Jan-2023 get SSE-S3 by default, but the dump does not prove which default the account applies.

Remediation: Set bucket default encryption explicitly (SSE-KMS for regulated data) so the posture is declared, not defaulted.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html

### `AF-GW-008` — Interface VPC endpoint without private DNS (medium)

`PrivateDnsEnabled: false` on an interface endpoint forces callers onto the endpoint-specific DNS name — code written against the public service DNS silently bypasses the private path.

Remediation: Enable private DNS when the endpoint is meant to serve the service's canonical name inside the VPC.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints.html
